curation.lead:
Carbyne (originally Reporty Ltd.) was an Israeli emergency-response surveillance technology company that received at least $3.6 million from Jeffrey Epstein's network through a deliberately concealed investment structure. Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak served as chairman and secured a carried interest in the investment vehicle, while Darren Indyke managed transactions through Southern Trust Company (STC), a US Virgin Islands entity. When Israeli lawyers handling anti-money-laundering compliance requested identification of the controlling person for the investment, Indyke wrote: "I thought we did not want your name associated with this Investment" (Finding #331). Epstein ultimately authorized disclosure of his ownership on March 14, 2019 — four months before his arrest.

The investment flowed through a multi-jurisdictional architecture: STC wired $1 million from account #9244 to ERGO Ltd. at Bank Leumi Israel on March 16, 2015, with reference "Reporty Investment" (Finding #328). The full $3.6 million structure involved SUM (E.B.) Limited Partnership acquiring warrants for 61,251 Preferred A Shares, with STC contributing 66.67% ($2.4M) and Nicole Junkermann's Montilla International Corporation contributing 33.33% ($1.2M) (Finding #330). The transaction also channeled through Deutsche Bank — the same institution later fined $150 million for Epstein-related compliance failures — with Indyke requesting that Richard Kahn obtain a bank recommendation letter from Stewart Oldfield at DB (Finding #335). Axon Enterprise acquired Carbyne in Q4 2025.

Carbyne maintained active US lobbying operations from Q3 2021 through Q4 2025, filing 19 disclosure reports through LSN Partners LLC focused on Next Generation 911 and emergency communications legislation including the SAVE Act (Finding #413). Notably, despite being an Israeli surveillance technology company with an Israeli intelligence figure as chairman, Carbyne had no Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing — unlike comparable Israeli firm NSO Group (Finding #393). The company also secured connections to Peter Thiel's Founders Fund through Junkermann's introduction of Carbyne CEO Amir Elichai to Trae Stephens, formerly of Palantir (Finding #340).

Did Carbyne's emergency response technology products receive procurement contracts from US government agencies, and if so, which agencies and under what compliance frameworks?

What was the nature of the 'intelligence' connections referenced in the Qatar pitch to Hamad bin Jassim Al Thani for World Cup 2022 security, and did Carbyne have formal relationships with Israeli intelligence services?
Why did Carbyne not file FARA registrations when comparable Israeli surveillance companies NSO Group and Q Cyber Technologies did, and what legal advice supported this position?
What due diligence did Axon Enterprise conduct regarding the Epstein-Barak investment history prior to the Q4 2025 acquisition, and were representations made about beneficial ownership?
curation.system_role: Carbyne reveals how the network operationalized jurisdictional arbitrage to conceal beneficial ownership: USVI entities for opacity, Israeli banks for operational distance, and Deutsche Bank as a compliance-willing bridge. The AML evasion tactics and absence of FARA registration demonstrate how intelligence-adjacent commercial ventures could operate in the US without standard foreign agent disclosure.

sections.title: Key Relationships
sections.content:
The Carbyne investment structure created interlocking relationships between Epstein's financial infrastructure, Israeli intelligence figures, and European investors. Ehud Barak served as chairman of Carbyne and held a carried interest through SUM (E.B.) Limited Partnership, the investment vehicle holding Carbyne warrants (Finding #330). In January 2016, Nicole Junkermann asked Epstein directly: "Ehud is interested in a carry (of course) how much would you give him?" — with NJF Capital modeling scenarios showing Barak's carry would range from $695,000 at a $100 million valuation to $1.97 million at a $200 million valuation (Finding #333).

Junkermann functioned as a critical network bridge, connecting the Epstein-Barak investment to Silicon Valley capital. In May 2018, she brokered an introduction between Carbyne CEO Amir Elichai and Trae Stephens at Founders Fund, the venture capital firm founded by Peter Thiel (Finding #340). Junkermann reported back to Epstein and Barak: "We made the connection to Founders Forum from Peter Thiel." The email chain shows both Epstein and Barak were CC'd throughout, with Chris Hopkins of NW/RIF Capital facilitating the connection and noting Stephens' "background at Palantir" and expected "serendipity." This placed an Israeli surveillance technology company with Epstein-Barak backing into direct conversation with Thiel's network of intelligence-adjacent technology investors.

On the financial infrastructure side, Darren Indyke served as the operational manager for Epstein's Carbyne investment, executing the STC wire transfers and handling AML compliance requests from Israeli lawyers (Finding #331). Richard Kahn was enlisted to obtain Deutsche Bank documentation, with Indyke noting Kahn had "a decent relationship" with Stewart Oldfield at DB (Finding #335). The investment thus drew upon the core Epstein-Indyke-Kahn relationship network that managed his broader financial operations.

sections.title: Financial Activity
sections.content:
The Carbyne investment structure was designed to obscure Epstein's beneficial ownership while maintaining his economic interest. On March 16, 2015, Darren Indyke wired $1 million from Southern Trust Company account #9244 to ERGO Ltd. at Bank Leumi Israel, with wire instructions specifying "Reporty Investment" as the reference (Finding #328). The full investment ultimately totaled $3.6 million, structured through SUM (E.B.) Limited Partnership holding warrants to purchase 61,251 Preferred A Shares. STC contributed $2.4 million (66.67%) while Montilla International Corporation — an entity associated with Nicole Junkermann's NJF Capital — contributed $1.2 million (33.33%) (Finding #330).

The investment was channeled through Deutsche Bank, with Indyke referencing "the transferring bank which is DB" in communications regarding compliance documentation (Finding #335). This linked the Carbyne transaction to the same banking relationship that would later result in a $150 million regulatory fine for Deutsche Bank's handling of Epstein accounts. In March 2019, when Israeli lawyers requested a bank recommendation letter for AML purposes, Indyke asked Richard Kahn to contact Stewart Oldfield at Deutsche Bank, noting that Kahn had "a decent relationship" with Oldfield.

The AML compliance process generated documentary evidence of deliberate ownership concealment. When Israeli lawyers handling the warrants exercise requested identification of the controlling person for anti-money-laundering purposes, Indyke wrote: "Not sure how to respond. I thought we did not want your name associated with this Investment?" (Finding #331). Barak reassured Epstein that the request reflected "Israeli banks paranoia after they paid the penalties...it was never leaked out of the banks." Epstein ultimately gave "ok" to disclose on March 14, 2019 — just four months before his July 2019 arrest. The fully exercised position would have increased SUM holdings from approximately 13% to 26.33% of Carbyne on a fully diluted basis.

From Q3 2021 through Q4 2025, Carbyne Inc. maintained active lobbying operations in the United States through LSN Partners LLC, filing 19 quarterly disclosure reports (Finding #413). Lobbying focused exclusively on Next Generation 911 and emergency communications legislation, including the Build Back Better Act, H.R.59 SAVE Act, and H.R.637 SAVE Act. Spending remained steady at $10,000 per quarter through Q3 2023, increasing to $20,000 per quarter from Q4 2024. Jose Fuentes served as the consistent lobbyist throughout the engagement, with lobbying continuing through Axon Enterprise's Q4 2025 acquisition of Carbyne.

sections.title: Regulatory Gaps
sections.content:
Carbyne's operational history reveals significant gaps in US regulatory coverage for foreign-owned surveillance technology companies. Despite being an Israeli company with an Israeli intelligence figure (Ehud Barak) as chairman, Carbyne maintained no Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing (Finding #393). This absence is particularly notable given comparable Israeli surveillance firm NSO Group and its parent company Q Cyber Technologies both maintained active FARA registrations through multiple US law firms. Carbyne's business model — providing emergency response and location-tracking technology to US government agencies — would typically trigger FARA disclosure requirements when foreign principals are involved in policy advocacy.

The AML compliance resistance documented in March 2019 (Finding #331) demonstrates how beneficial ownership information can be systematically withheld even when regulatory frameworks technically require disclosure. Darren Indyke's initial response to Israeli bank requests — "I thought we did not want your name associated with this Investment" — reveals that concealment was the default preference, with disclosure only authorized when the transaction could not proceed otherwise. Barak's characterization of Israeli bank AML requirements as "paranoia" following regulatory penalties suggests an operational culture that viewed compliance obligations as obstacles to be managed rather than requirements to be met.
